A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, figures, tables, proofs, and experimental appendices. Renumbered and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic graph experiments in Figures 1–2 and molecular regression results on ZINC and QM9 in Table 2.

after.justification: v2 reports synthetic and molecular experiments, including additional parameter-efficient implementation results in Appendix 15, Figure 3.

M1.justification: The main architectures and losses remain unchanged. However, v2 Appendix 11 drops the leading minus sign on W^V in Corollary 7's explicit construction, present in v1 Appendix 9. This locally changes the specified weights and conflicts with the still-stated μI−L update; it does not establish a change to the trained models.

E1.justification: Both versions use ten-node fully connected and Circular Skip Links graphs for electric-flow, resistive-embedding, heat-kernel, and eigenvector tasks, plus ZINC and QM9 molecular regression. Figure 3 evaluates another implementation within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: Section 5 and Appendix 15 newly compare the parameter-efficient implementation with the standard linear-Transformer implementation on the synthetic objectives. Table 2 retains the same Graph Transformer without PE and Graph Transformer with LapPE comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix 15 adds a controlled architecture comparison: Figure 3 uses the corresponding Figures 1 and 2(d) settings while substituting the parameter-efficient implementation. Existing graph sampling, molecular splits, model dimensions, pretraining, learning rates, and training budgets remain unchanged as documented.

E4.justification: Figure 3 adds an architecture ablation testing whether parameter constraints preserve accuracy across four synthetic objectives. The existing depth sweeps and analyses of individual eigenvector errors remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify means and standard deviations from four independent seeded runs for Table 2. Synthetic plots contain shaded bands in both versions; v2 introduces no new uncertainty-estimation procedure, significance test, or synthetic run-count disclosure.

E6.justification: Figure 1 replaces the three synthetic loss curves under the same reported setup. For example, nine-layer CSL electric-flow log loss changes from approximately −5.5 to −10.7, reversing its ordering relative to FC. Figure 3 adds four objectives' parameter-efficient results. Figure 2 and Table 2 remain unchanged, but the synthetic numerical evidence is substantially revised.

T1.justification: Lemma 1 restores layer-count dependence in its exponential bound and removes an extra demand-norm factor; its contraction derivation is expanded. Algorithm 1 now orthogonalizes the updated iterate, and Section 4 relaxes the stated initialization from column-orthogonal to full column rank. The theorem suite is retained, while Corollary 7's proof acquires a missing-minus-sign error.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same central claims: explicit Transformer constructions for graph algorithms, corresponding approximation guarantees, parameter-efficient implementation, and learned positional encodings for molecular regression. Additional validation does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: The discussion of Lemma 6 now attributes the difficult convergence-rate dependence specifically to spectral gaps of Φ0; v1 referred only to pairwise spectral gaps. No new convergence analysis supports that specificity. The eigenvector-learning interpretations, QM9/ZINC explanation, and non-SOTA qualification otherwise remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit project-code repository link in the abstract. Its new Reproducibility section mainly points to existing methodological details; the detailed molecular architecture, optimizer settings, training schedules, and seeded-run information were already present in v1.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 adds discussion and citations concerning learned positional encodings and structural representations: Dwivedi et al. (2021), Mialon et al. (2021), Eliasof et al. (2023), Park et al. (2022), and Srinivasan and Ribeiro (2020). The paper's principal positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized rewrites to the abstract, preliminaries, and explanatory passages, updates affiliations and acknowledgements, and adds Ethics Statement and Reproducibility sections. The main narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The document is extensively retypeset into the ICLR format, changing margins, heading styles, headers, float placement, and figure sizing throughout. Table 1 moves earlier, Figure 1 receives revised axes and legends, and a new four-panel Figure 3 is added.

improvement.justification: Figure 3 adds a useful controlled test of parameter efficiency, and the code link improves reproducibility information. Corrections to Lemma 1 and Algorithm 1 also improve consistency. These provide a modest net gain, tempered by the newly missing minus sign in Corollary 7's construction, which weakens that proof's reliability.
